reasons.reader_question: The chapter ends on a concrete gap: will a human-hands marma strike in the kalari pit work, and is Devan even there at the hour the fort believes? It is close to the beat's question, but the closing hitch sentence blurs whether the reader carries 'can she' or 'will she'.
reasons.change: Knowledge and power both shift. She sees that the barred shutters turn any beast kill into a hanging for the bride, so the beast plan dies and a new plan replaces it. The value shift 'window open -> a plan he has quietly made impossible' lands cleanly.
reasons.romance_movement: The romance moves for a new reason. Over his throat she ends up reading his scarred hand, nearly touches it with her muzzle, and looks back, 'which she did not do'. Her tactical excuse is visibly thinning, as the beat requires, though he never responds awake.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Attraction is shown through action and attention: counting his knuckle scars, whiskers trembling at his wrist, his fingers curling a finger's width from her nose. The reader knows from earlier chapters that he may be feigning sleep, which charges the moment. Nothing is narrated as chemistry.
reasons.character_logic: She argues the bar both ways like a professional and correctly abandons the beast kill. One weakness: she rediscovers her doubt about his dawn rising as if it were new, when she already noted it in ch6 (F078), which makes her look slower than she is.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: Practical costs are named: the ache counts a skipped night, it is his ground, she gets one strike, and Ammu is Chathu's coin. The emotional cost of a bare-handed kill after the hand moment is never felt at dawn; the plan is called 'good' and the hand vanishes from her mind.
reasons.prose: Concrete and sensory, with no banned phrases, no em-dash overuse and good rhythm (the 'Forty-five. Forty-six.' hook works). Tics recur, though: 'She did not like' appears twice here and twice in ch9, and 'told herself' appears three times. 'Gone queer from the damp' may jar a modern reader.
reasons.continuity: Conflict with F322: Janu is established as the source of the damp-madness theory, but here Bhaskaran's lads say damp and Janu says 'shy'. Everything else checks out against the bible and facts: 31 nights, Raiu at the stair head, unlit lamp, pulled sentry, kindi spout toward the pillow, sword hilt-first, the breath hitch, the ginger tom, the clause read two days ago.

fixes: Continuity (F322 conflict). At "I say shy. Shy men bolt doors." Janu must own the damp theory. Give Bhaskaran's lads the privacy or new-wife theory, and Chinna whatever is left. Have Janu say something like "I say it's the damp. It gets into a man's head up here." Then cut or rework Neela's "He doesn't strike me as shy" exchange so it answers damp (e.g. "He doesn't strike me as damp." / "He doesn't strike you as anything, he's a locked chest"). Keep "Ask him" as Janu's push.

Repetitive tension / character logic. At "Janu said he rose in the last dark hour. Neela had never seen it." she rediscovers a doubt she already logged in ch6 (F078). Rewrite it as accumulated evidence: this is the third or fourth first light she has found him abed, and she has been explaining it away. The snag then becomes her admitting she has been relying on Janu's story for a week, a sharper self-indictment. Cut "She did not like any of the three." so the paragraph ends on the decision.

Stakes and cost. At "It was a good plan. She told it to the kindi" the hand moment from the night scene drops out of her head entirely, so the new plan costs her nothing emotionally. Add one or two lines where, as she pictures the strike at 'the door', the scarred right hand comes up unbidden: either as the hand that would block her, or as the thing she would be ending. She files it as tactics, the way she filed 'no beast could carry this kill'. This keeps the romance cost alive into the cliff and earns the beat's 'tactical reason wearing thin'.
reader_question: Can Neela kill Devan with her bare hands in his own kalari pit before dawn, when she isn't even sure he is there at that hour?
new_facts_assessment: F361 (marma 'the door', a thumb's width below the skull): necessary. It sets up ch11 and matches F347, where Devan says she put her fingers at the base of his skull. Keep it. F362 (seven knuckle scars and the thumb line on the right hand): consistent with his solo drilling and his eight years without sparring, it pays forward to the loss of his right hand in book 3, and it gives the beat's 'old scars' a specific reading. Keep it. F363 (at first light she sees him abed and resolves to scout the pit): consistent with F078 and F309, and it bridges into ch11. However, F078 already records this same doubt at first light in ch6, so the snag is a recycled discovery rather than a new fact. It should be framed as confirmation of an earlier unease, not a fresh surprise.
